Question: A client withdrew 40% last month and the portfolio is now below our composite minimum. Must we remove it?
Jurisdiction: JN
As of: 2025-06-01
Facts stated: withdrawal: 40% of assets; portfolio below composite minimum: yes
Unresolved in the question: withdrawal date: 'last month' (no anchor date given); composite minimum: amount not specified

EVIDENCE IN FORCE (citable):
- [prov:composite-minimum@E2025] 3.A.7 — provision, authoritative, obligation: must; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    If a firm sets a minimum asset level for portfolios to be included in a composite, the firm must not include portfolios below that minimum. Any such minimum must be documented and applied consistently.
- [gs:GS-2025-02@v1] GS-2025-02 — interpretive guidance, interpretive, obligation: n/a; Guidance Statement GS-2025-02 — Composite Minimums; in force from 2025-03-01
    Provision 3.A.7 requires that portfolios below a documented composite minimum not be included in the composite. Firms should assess each portfolio against the minimum at the beginning of each measurement period, using the valuation methodology documented in the composite policy. A portfolio that is above the minimum at the beginning of a measurement period is included for that period in its entirety. Where the firm changes a composite minimum, the change applies prospectively from the beginning of the next measurement period (see also recommendation 3.B.1). Where a portfolio falls below the minimum solely as a result of a significant cash flow, the Board has addressed the treatment of such temporary breaches in Q&A QA-2025-031.
- [def:composite@E2025] 1.D.1 — definition, authoritative, obligation: definition; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy.
- [def:measurement-period@E2025] 1.D.10 — definition, authoritative, obligation: definition; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    The calendar month, unless the firm's documented policy for a composite specifies a shorter period.
- [def:significant-cash-flow@E2025] 1.D.11 — definition, authoritative, obligation: definition; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    A significant cash flow is a client-directed external cash flow of a size, defined in the firm's documented policy for the composite, that would temporarily prevent the firm from implementing the composite strategy.
- [def:external-cash-flow@E2025] 1.D.9 — definition, authoritative, obligation: definition; GSB Standards, Edition 2025; in force from 2025-01-01
    Capital, in cash or investments, that enters or exits a portfolio at the direction of the client.

REFERENCED BUT NOT HELD (do not guess contents):
- Q&A QA-2025-031 — Temporary breach of a composite minimum following a significant cash flow — referenced by gs:GS-2025-02; no text held in this release

summary.description: One sentence answering the question directly.

response.summary: Generally yes for the current period if it was below the documented minimum at the start of that period, but it stays in for the period in which the withdrawal occurred, and separate unreviewed Board Q&A on significant cash flows may change the outcome.

claims.text: Removal depends on when the portfolio is assessed against the minimum and whether the withdrawal is a significant cash flow under your composite policy.
Under 3.A.7, if the firm sets a composite minimum, it must not include portfolios below that minimum.
Under 3.A.7, any composite minimum must be documented and applied consistently.
GS-2025-02 says firms should assess each portfolio against the minimum at the beginning of each measurement period, using the valuation methodology in the composite policy.
Under 1.D.10, a measurement period is the calendar month, unless your documented composite policy sets a shorter period.
If the portfolio was above the minimum at the start of the period in which the withdrawal occurred, GS-2025-02 says it is included for that entire period.
If the portfolio is below the minimum at the start of a later measurement period, 3.A.7 means it must not be included for that period.
Under 1.D.9, a client-directed withdrawal is an external cash flow.
Under 1.D.11, a withdrawal is a significant cash flow only if it meets the size threshold in your composite policy and would temporarily prevent implementing the strategy.

GS-2025-02 says the treatment of temporary breaches caused solely by a significant cash flow is addressed in Q&A QA-2025-031. That Q&A is not held and has not been reviewed, so it may affect whether removal is required.
The exact withdrawal date and the minimum amount were not given, so it is not possible to confirm which measurement periods are affected.
